items.title: Jamison Savage [Caturra Washed]
items.desc:
Le Panama ne produit simplement de superbes Geishas, parce que au milieu de cette obsession pour les tasses emplie de clarté et de pureté, il existe des cafés beaucoup plus directs, plus gourmands, tout en restant équilibrés. Ce Caturra Lavé de Jamison Savage en fait partie.
La tasse commence sur quelque chose de gourmand : le chocolat au lait, puis arrive la prune rouge, avec cette sensation vive et élégante que l’on retrouve dans les cafés kenyans. Enfin, ces notes s’élargissent vers la noisette, en laissant une sensation douce et généreuse en bouche. Un Caturra qui ne cherche pas à jouer au

items.title: Los Lajones Porton [GN #23109]
items.desc: Notre lot Geisha Naturel 23109 provient de Los Lajones, la ferme de Graciano Cruz, dans la région de Boquete au Panama. La propriété en elle-même est très très intéressante. Une grande partie de son territoire reste couverte de forêt, et les plantations de café occupent notamment les secteurs plus élévés. Graciano Cruz a une approche construite autour des procédés classiques de traitement, avec une volonté de travailler le café sans chercher à le rendre artificiellement spectaculaire. Le principe est plutôt de donner au fruit et à la variété suffisamment de temps pour exprimer ce qu’ils ont a

items.title: Hacienda la Esmeralda [Lino 6HC]
items.desc:
Cultivé à haute altitude dans la région de Boquete, au Panama, au sein de la célèbre Hacienda la Esmeralda, le café Lino 6HC bénéficie d’un procédé honey avec séchage contrôlé, où le séchage des cerises avec une partie de mucilage est maîtrisé afin de préserver la complexité aromatique tout en développant douceur et profondeur. Le nom Lino ne désigne pas une variété, mais un bien lot spécifique de la ferme, en isolant des parcelles précises, Hacienda la Esmeralda vient chercher à isoler les expressions les plus intéressantes du terroir.

items.title: Finca Sophia [RW4 – Colibri-Poro 40 GW] – Auction Lot
items.desc:
L’équipe de Tanat Coffee est honorée de partager avec vous deux lots obtenus lors de la vente aux enchères de la Finca Sophia. Deux cafés Geisha lavés exceptionnels, qui témoignent de notre admiration pour l’engagement, la rigueur et la passion de l’équipe Finca Sophia.
Ces deux lots lavés vous feront découvrir deux profils sensoriels authentiques, mettant en valeur la pureté de la variété, le soin apporté à son terroir ainsi que la maîtrise d’un procédé de lavage d’une extrême précision.
Une acidité d’agrumes douce et vive ouvre sur des notes de mandarine, de nectarine, de bonbon au citron et

items.title: Elto [Hamasho 96h]
items.desc:
Sur les hauts plateaux de Bensa, en Éthiopie, se trouve Elto Coffee, projet d’Eliyas Dukamo et d’Atiklit Dejene. Forts tous deux d’une solide expérience dans la production de cafés d’exception en Éthiopie, ils ont créé Elto Coffee avec l’ambition de repousser les standards de qualité en mettant la lumière les terroirs de Bensa et des méthodes de lavage plus modernes.
Sur notre lot Elto Hamasho, les 96 heures de fermentation construisent une tasse d’une intensité forte, mais toujours lisible. En début de dégustation, les fruits noirs prennent la main, une myrtille juteuse, une mûre éclatante, u

items.title: Alo [Digs Project Anaerobic Honey 48h]
items.desc:
Direction les hauts plateaux de Bensa, au coeur du village d’Alo, où le producteur Tamiru Tadesse signe des cafés parmi les plus recherché d’Éthiopie. Ce lot est issu d’une fermentation anaérobie honey avec 48h de fermentation. Les cerises sont sélectionnées minutieusement avant de fermenter en environnement anaérobie pendant deux jours, permettant un développement aromatique intense ; après cette fermentation contrôlée, le café est dépulpé puis séché lentement sur lits africains, avec une partie du mucilage préservée pour apporter d’avantage de sucrosité.

items.title: Gesha Village [Oma Anaerobic Natural 26/E24]
items.desc:
Issu de mythique terroir de Gesha Village, au coeur de la région de West Omo en Éthiopie, ce lot Oma G26 E24 est cultivé sur les pentes du bloc Oma, où la variété Gesha 1931 exprime tpute sa finesse. La fermentation en anaérobie naturelle de ce lot apporte une profondeur aromatique remarquable sans masquer l’identité du terroir.
En tasse, l’ouverture est aérienne. Le coquelicot vient évoquer une douceur florale, rejoint par une myrtille juteuse et l’orange vient ensuite illuminer l’ensemble d’une fraîcheur vive, laissant une finale longue et élégante.
Chaque tasse évoluera en refroidissant, dé

items.title: Janson [Hacienda GW121]
items.desc:
Découvrez ce magnifique lot 121 Geisha lavé issue de la plantation Hacienda Janson. Il se dévoilera en tasse un café expressif et pur, caractéristique des hauts plateaux de la région de Chiriqui, au Panama, nichée sur les hauts plateaux de Volcan.
Un café d’une grande douceur et élégance, sa texture soyeuse, sa finesse florale rappelant le chèvrefeuille et sa finale longue abricot en font un grand cru d’exception.

items.title: Alo Bore [Washed]
items.desc:
Ce lot vient des hauteurs du Guji, en Éthiopie, où Tamiru Tadesse cultive la variété 74158 à plus de 2000 mètres d’altitude.
Traité en lavé, il offre une tasse nette et florale, où les fleurs blanches laissent place à la pêche, avant une finale vive de pamplemousse.

items.title: Choco Nuts
items.desc: Choco Nuts is our latest Brazilian espresso, produced by Adriano Muñiz and his family at Agropecuária Muñiz in Sul de Minas. This anaerobic natural Catucaí has everything we enjoy in a classic Brazilian coffee, with plenty of sweetness, a round body and a creamy texture. Expect notes of hazelnut, milk chocolate and vanilla, making it a great everyday espresso that also works really well with milk.

items.title: Pillow Talk
items.desc: Los Nogales does decaf a little differently. This Caturra is grown, processed and decaffeinated at the farm in Pitalito, giving Oscar Hernandez and his team control over the coffee from cherry to finished decaf. It’s bright and sweet, with starfruit, agave and rosemary. A decaf we’d happily drink whether we were looking for one or not. * Due to the decaffeination process, the beans may have an unusual colour. This is completely normal and does not affect the quality of the coffee.

items.title: Peachy Daze
items.desc: Peachy Daze is back, a clean washed Ethiopian from the Chelbesa washing station in Gedeb, where heirloom varieties grow at 2173 masl. The cup is light and delicate, with white peach and lemon up front, black tea through the middle and a soft elderflower finish.

items.title: Blackberry Dust
items.desc: Blackberry Dust is a late-harvest natural Ethiopian coffee from the Buku Abel washing station in Guji, which arrived in Europe just a few weeks ago. Around 400 smallholder farmers contribute to the station, growing heirloom varieties at elevations between 1,900 and 2,100 masl. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of blackberry, wild strawberry and blueberry yoghurt, followed by a soft, creamy finish.

items.title: Macaron
items.desc: One of our all-time favourites from Johan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, this natural Red Bourbon has become one of those coffees we’re always excited to bring back. It goes through an advanced anaerobic natural process and comes out big, juicy and seriously sweet, with strawberry jam, raspberry macaron and buttercream.

items.title: Sticky Pudding
items.desc: Our Christmas coffee is here! This year we’ve worked with CATA Export in Colombia to create something inspired by the festive season. This bourbon undergoes a co-fermentation with cinnamon, cardamom, mandarin and cherry, giving it a distinctive profile while keeping plenty of sweetness in the cup. Expect notes of cinnamon, cardamom and fresh fir – a very festive profile.

items.title: Cream Donut
items.desc: Cream Donut is a collaboration with Cata Export and producer Franky Hoyos in Colombia. A yeast-inoculated natural Caturra Chiroso developed for DAK through rounds of back-and-forth trialling. It’s an unusual coffee that has somehow become one of our staples and a bestseller, loved for its distinct character and the ridiculously good flat white it makes. Expect chocolate milk, cherry-filled doughnut and vanilla, whether you brew it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Plum Butter
items.desc: Plum Butter is a natural from Bulambuli in East Uganda, produced with our long-time partners at Ibero. It’s a profile we don’t come across often from Uganda: deep, smooth and fruit-forward, with dark plum, grape cordial and cacao. Rich without becoming too heavy.

items.title: Berry Blues
items.desc: Berry Blues is back. We’ve had this coffee in different variations over the years, sometimes under Berry Blues, sometimes as Blueberry Boom, and it remains a favourite across the DAK team for its big fruit character and how much fun it is to drink. This year’s harvest from Esayas Beriso is an anaerobic natural, grown high in Oromia, Ethiopia, and slowly dried in the shade. There’s plenty of dark fruit and a boozy edge: grape soda up front, myrtle liquor behind it, and a cashew-butter richness that gives the cup its buttery body and creamy mouthfeel.

items.title: Darling
items.desc: Darling comes from Danche Washing Station in Gedeb, and it’s one of the more delicate Ethiopians we’ve had this year. The coffee goes through a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation before being washed, resulting in a cup with good clarity despite the additional fermentation. Wild florals lead, followed by peach iced tea and a black-tea finish. Light, elegant and very tea-like.

items.title: Rhubarb Fizz
items.desc: Our next Kenyan of the season, and one of our favourites this year. Rhubarb Fizz is a washed AA from Ndimi Factory in Kirinyaga, bringing together SL28, SL34, Batian and Ruiru 11 from the surrounding smallholder farms. Juicy and layered, with rhubarb soda, blackcurrant and orange.

items.title: Hazel Nuts
items.desc: Hazel Nuts is a natural Catuaí from Chinacla in the Marcala region of Honduras, grown by our longtime partners Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera. We’ve been buying their coffees for years, and this is one we particularly like for espresso. Round and silky, with hazelnut, cacao nibs and blackberry, plus a touch of booziness that we really enjoy. Especially good with milk.

items.title: Silky Way
items.desc: Silky Way is another coffee from Jhoan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, the same family behind Macaron. This time it’s their washed Pink Bourbon, with a completely different side of the farm showing up in the cup. Lemongrass, white florals and crisp green apple, with a bright, sparkling quality that suits the name pretty well.

items.title: Poppy Soda
items.desc: Poppy Soda is a Pink Bourbon from Sebastián Ramírez at El Placer in Quindío, Colombia. It goes through a pretty elaborate washed process, but the cup itself is all about clarity. Lemonade, jasmine tea and ripe peach, with a bright, almost soda-like quality that makes the name make sense.

items.title: The Alchemist
items.desc: The Alchemist is one of the staples in our line-up and a coffee we source directly from Gasharu Farms in Nyamasheke, Rwanda. An anaerobic natural Red Bourbon that changes quite a bit depending on how you brew it. Espresso pushes the cacao forward; filter opens up the tropical fruit and jammy sweetness. Complex, rich and particularly good with milk.

items.title: Jazz fruits
items.desc: Jazz Fruits is a staple in our lineup and one we try to keep around all year, whenever the harvest allows. We source this community lot from Daye Bensa each year for its fruity, easy-going profile and how well it works as espresso, especially with milk. Strawberry, white chocolate and mandarin in the cup. Named after the Jazz Fruits playlists on Spotify.

items.title: Mucho Berry Blend
items.desc:
Mucho Berry
Momos Coffee’s fourth signature blend
Ethiopia is widely known as one of the coffee-growing regions loved by many people. In particular, Ethiopian coffees processed by the natural method are recognized for their diverse berry-like aromas and their broad appeal, making them enjoyable for a wide range of drinkers.
Inspired by these berry characteristics, the fourth signature blend, Mucho Berry, was created to express rich and attractive berry-forward aromas.

items.title: Fruity Bonbon Blend
items.desc:
Fruity Bonbon
Momos Coffee’s second signature blend
In 2009, when specialty coffee was first encountered in the United States, coffees with bright acidity and fruit-like aromas were still unfamiliar to many people. However, drawn to the diverse aromas and new flavors found in high-quality coffee, Momos Coffee introduced its second signature blend, Fruity Bonbon, to share the distinct character and appeal of specialty coffee.

items.title: Es Chocolat Blend
items.desc:
Es Chocolat
Momos Coffee’s first signature blend
Es Chocolat, the very first signature blend introduced by Momos Coffee, was developed at a time when dark-roasted coffees reminiscent of chocolate were the mainstream style. It reflects the early days of Momos Coffee and the intention to create a coffee that could be enjoyed and loved by everyone.

items.title: Apax Lab - Jamm
items.desc:
JAMM is formulated to bring roundness and will accentuate the lingering sweetness and creamy mouthfeel of your brew. With just a few drops, it enhances body and softens sharp edges, delivering a smooth and full-flavoured cup.
Used by World Coffee Champions and trusted by leading cafés worldwide , JAMM is the go-to profile for coffee enthusiasts looking to balance complex or funky coffees with ease.
Enhances body and mouthfeel
Increases sweetness and balance
Smooths sharp or funky notes
Perfect for naturals, experimental fermentations, and winey coffees

items.title: Apax Lab - Lylac
items.desc:
LYLAC is designed to extend the finish and highlight delicate aromatics in your coffee. It refines texture, reduces dryness, and reveals a silky, elegant cup with a long, clean aftertaste.
Favoured by coffee competitors and leading cafés worldwide , LYLAC is the secret weapon for showcasing refined coffees and elegant filter brews.
Highlights floral aromatics

The Chiroso variety is expanding rapidly in Colombia, and we're excited to bring in even more as new trees mature. items.desc:
Flavour Notes
black plum / chocolate truffle / dates / brandy
Sweetness ●●●●○ Acidity ●●●○○ Body ●●●●●
Hacienda Barbara Pacamara is a deep and indulgent coffee, with rich notes of black plum and chocolate truffle layered over syrupy dates and a subtle, brandy-like warmth. Its full body and gentle acidity create a velvety, luxurious cup with lingering sweetness and depth.

items.title: Second Slice / Costa Rica
items.desc: Second Slice is pure comfort in a cup. Warm cinnamon and baked apple pie bring the sweetness, while toasted pecan adds a rich, nutty finish. A cozy Costa Rican coffee that tastes like going back for another piece.

items.title: Cherry Wild / Colombia
items.desc:
Cherry Wild is a celebration of Colombia’s vibrant coffee spirit—lively, sweet, and just a little
untamed. Bursting with ripe cherry brightness, the cup carries the rich, spiced depth of fruitcake, lifted by a sparkling hint of tangerine.

items.title: Janson X Los Alpes Washed Geisha Lot 536
items.desc:
Flavour Notes
jasmine / grapefruit / mandarin orange / white tea
Sweetness ●●●●○ Acidity ●●●●● Body ●●●○○
Janson X Los Alpes Washed Geisha Lot 536 is a delicate and vibrant coffee, featuring fragrant jasmine, zesty grapefruit, and sweet mandarin orange, with a refined white tea-like finish. Its crisp acidity and silky body create an elegant and refreshing cup.
This lot is processed using the Janson X drying method, which combines advanced technology with traditional techniques for precise and consistent drying. After the washed process, where cherries are depulped, fermented, and fully washed,

items.title: Hideaway / Dark
items.desc: Hideaway is your go-to dark roast for those moments when only the richest, most comforting coffee will do.

items.title: Daydream / Light
items.desc:
Let your thoughts drift with Daydream.
Daydream is your invitation to pause and reflect, perfect for moments when you need a gentle lift.

items.title: Two Wheel / House
items.desc:
Kick start your day with a dynamic ride.
Two Wheel is like a morning ride through your favourite part of town, energizing and full of life.

items.title: Off Hours / Decaf Coffee
items.desc:
Unwind anytime with a decaf that’s rich in flavour, without the caffeine.
Off Hours is perfect for those late-night moments or anytime you need a break without the buzz; it’s decaf done right.

items.title: Homebody / Medium
items.desc: Homebody is like your favourite spot on the couch – always welcoming and perfectly cozy, ideal for thriving in your safe space.

items.title: KENYA Gondo AA
items.desc:
Gondo AA comes from Gondo Factory in Murang’a County, on the western slopes of the Aberdare Mountains. The factory is one of three managed by the New Kiriti Farmers Cooperative Society, and it receives cherry from 727 smallholder farmers in the surrounding area. Most farms are small, often averaging around 250 coffee trees, and the cool temperatures, regular rainfall, and deep red volcanic soils help the coffee mature slowly.

items.title: COLOMBIA La Violeta Sidra
items.desc:
La Violeta is one of Rafael Aya Martínez’s farms in La Florida, near Timaná in southern Huila. This year, we stayed overnight on the farm, walked the land with Rafael, cupped through his coffees together, and visited his new café in Timaná. The visit gave us a clearer view of how his work connects cultivation, processing, and the local coffee culture he is helping build around his own coffees.

items.title: ETHIOPIA Esayas Beriso
items.desc:
The Manos Juntas micromill can be found in the Sotara area of Colombia’s Cauca region.
The region stretches from the western Cordillera Mountains to the Pacific Ocean and is characterized by the Popayan plateau, many rivers, and the central volcanic mountain range.
Operated and managed by Banexport, the micromill’s entire concept is based on simplifying tasks and responsibilities, for both the producers and Banexport.

items.title: GUATEMALA Buena Vista Pacamara Natural
items.desc:
In the Fraijanes region of Guatemala, close to the city of Santa Rosa, the Buena Vista farm is located. The humid climate of the Fraijanes plateau with its sunny afternoons makes for the perfect combination for coffee plants to thrive and subsequently be fully sun-dried.

items.title: Hanan Million Natural | Guji, Ethiopia
items.desc:
Local landrace varieties carrying the particular character of Buku Hambella. Hanan founded ASHKIM with her mother, Asha Yuya, the name honouring Asha and her sister Kimiya.
The fermentation that happens inside a drying coffee fruit is microbially complex and environmentally responsive, and the difference between a natural that sings and one that doesn't comes down to decisions made on the drying bed across weeks. Hanan's lands in the expressive register: purple haribo gummies, bubblegum, white tea are things we’ve been picking up with this one.

items.title: Moata Raya Lunar Honey | Agaro, Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is a fun experiment using 74110 local landrace (and catalogued by JARC) grown by smallholder farmers on garden plots in Agaro. Moata bought this fruit from locals as he doesn't have a farm, but he still wanted to work through this processing idea - and we get to enjoy the results together. This lot is a honey, where Moata used a hand disk pulper with no further soak, and laid the parchment out on raised beds, covered with shade mesh during the day, and opening the netting at dusk and overnight, resulting in things like nougaty white mulberry, taffy and oolong.

items.title: Basha Bekele Natural (minis) | Sidama, Ethiopia
items.desc: Variety 74158 grown by 1st place COE winner (2024), Basha Bekele, on his farm in Bombe, Bensa, Sidama. Proccessed as a natural with whole fruit dried on raised beds. This lot is particularily special as it features the smallest screen sizes, not normally exportable. Moata, who works with Crop to Cup took it upon himself to painstakingly re-sort these 'minis', with the idea that these smaller fruits have outsized flavour. We're inclined to agree.

items.title: Janson Washed Geisha #232
items.desc:
Kai and Jannette Janson are the main people behind Janson Family Estates - and are two of the loveliest people in Panama. They've been running the operations at the farm, located in the town of Volcan, for many years now - preceded by generations in the Janson family.
This coffee is grown at their HACSA farm, around 1600m, which is right behind their processing factory, and offers amazing growing conditions for their Green Tip Geisha.
This particular lot was sorted for ripe cherries only. It was fermented for 48 hours in cherry before being depulped, washed, and dried on raised beds for 10 day

items.title: Danche Hydro Honey
items.desc: We're welcoming in a new lot that we haven't worked with this producer before, and we've got to say - it's something very special! This is from the Danche Washing Station, in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, very closely located to the Chelbesa stations. The cherry here is sourced from 810 registered growers in the villages Danche and Kubi, in Gedeo zone, Gedeb. The average elevation of the farms lies at around 2100 Meters Above Sea level on rich and fertile red soil in a semi-forested environment, and harvest takes place between November and January. Cherry variety is Mixed Heirloom / Ethiopian Land Ra

items.title: Kiandu AA Washed
items.desc:
Great, classic washed Kenyan coffees are getting harder and harder to find unfortunately. Subtle changes to farming practices, environmental reasons, and changes to varieties mean that the classic Kenyan profile of old is much more rare. This Kiandu AA lot is a great representation of how great and fruity Kenyan Washed coffees can be!
Kiandu is a high-quality washing station in the Tetu area of Nyeri County, on the southern slopes of Mount Kenya. It operates under the Mutheka Farmers Cooperative Society (locally also known as Kiandu FCS), which runs several factories in the region and supports

items.title: Bambito Estate Geisha Washed (Competition Lot)
items.desc:
Ever since first trying Ivan and Priscilla's coffee's in 2022, we loved what they produced. Their elusive Washed Geisha is a rare lot that speaks for itself in quality and elegance - something super special, and worth appreciating!
Grown in Bambito, nearby Volcan in Panama (just off the road leading to Cerro Punta), the land where their geisha grows goes up the mountain to around 1800m above sea level. There's a beautiful forest that sits around the top part of their Geisha, which is very peaceful to walk through. Their Geisha grows well here, and in this terroir they're already producing grea

items.title: Alo Main Station Dark Room Dry Natural
items.desc:
From the main station of Alo Village, and a producer we've worked with for several years now, comes a very special lot that represents how much Tamiru Tadesse has pushed processing at Alo. This lot is a classic natural, without extra fermentation but has a special dark room drying. Tamiru built these dark rooms for drying coffee a few years ago, but has expanded them recently to accomodate more lots, and we were lucky enough to get this one, lot #34. This whole 17kg lot has been sent to us, and we're happy to share it with you now.
The coffee itself is grown at over 2400m above sea level, alre

items.title: Mama Sierra Caturra Washed
items.desc:
This is your answer to a daily coffee that's good on price, giving a dependable flavour profile, and enjoyable every day without being too much. Mama Sierra, led by Sirley Pulgarin of The Coffee Quest Colombia, is a remarkable project empowering women coffee farmers in the community of Giraldo, Antioquia. With 15 motivated members, the project began in March 2021, initiated by Yessica Parra and later taken forward by Sirley. The goal has always been to break barriers limiting women’s access to resources and training in coffee production.
This lot is a Caturra with a classic washed process from

items.title: Kotowa Las Brujas Geisha Clean Natural
items.desc:
This year is the first year we're buying from Kotowa Farms in Boquete, and we're absolutely thrilled to offer this amazing Geisha from their Las Brujas farm lot 26-094!
This lot in particular is their outstanding Geisha, which was processed with a "Natural" process, although the result in the cup is something that reminds us much more of a washed. We had confirmed with the farm that it was infact a natural, even though it does appear more washed. This coffee was picked on the 3rd of February, and left in bags overnight before being laid straight onto raised african beds, spread into a thin 5cm

items.title: Chilaka Anaerobic Natural
items.desc:
Tamiru Tadesse is a coffee supplier who has been in the coffee business for the last eight years. He works with about 200 farmers in Delo Kebele, Bensa zone of the Sidama region. He collects about 182,000 kilograms of red cherry from an estimated 80 hectares of land owned by the farmers. Tamiru processes anaerobic and natural coffee which is dried on a raised bed with mesh wire. He then sells his coffee on the international market, mostly in China. However, he says, he was interested to have new market destinations and promote the unique flavours of Bensa coffee.
This particular lot is from th

items.title: Altieri Pre-dry Natural Geisha DFM
items.desc:
This is our first year visiting and buying from the Altieri farm in Boquete, and it was an absolute treat. Getting to see their facilities, and cup their outstanding lots from a variety of processes and elevations is really impressive! We purchased a few lots from them, and the first to be released is this pre-dry natural Geisha.
This lot is from their Tom lot - it sits around 1700m above sea level at Alto Quiel, in Boquete, Panama. It covers an area of approximately 1 hectare of volcanic soil where Geisha Green Tip grows. It is adjacent to the protected area of the Volcan Baru national park,

items.title: Guji Rassa Washed
items.desc:
This is a classic washed Ethiopian coffee that ticks all the boxes. You can imagine that when someone says "washed Ethiopian coffee" you have a profile in mind - this is exactly that - nothing more, nothing less.
Grown from 2000-2200masl in the village of Rassa, in the Guji region of Ethiopia, this lot is comprised of mixed heirloom varieties without specific selection of varieties that comes with several smallholder farmers producing cherries at a time. The cherries are sent to the Suke Washing station where they're processed in the traditional washed fashion - floated, depulped, washed, and

items.title: Chiroso Washed Las Perlitas
items.desc:
A washed Chiroso from Las Perlitas in Antioquia, Colombia, sourced through Coffee Quest. Smallholder deliveries are cupped separately and combined when their profiles complement one another.
Bright, juicy and sweet, with orange, prune and almond in the cup. We roast it to work beautifully as both filter and espresso.

items.title: Cherry Ripe Blend
items.desc:
This coffee is born out of a simple question - how can we make an espresso blend that's the most fruity as possible, while still being clear and clean. We have been working on this lot for several months, starting right from sourcing. We worked hand in hand with our friends at Cofinet to source these components and design this blend around 3 particular lots.
Firstly a Washed and Natural Caturra - these set the base for our blend providing a fruity, yet well structured base. The last component is a small amount of a Cherry co-fermented coffee from Jairo Arcilla. This is what gives us that big b

items.title: Rose Rejects
items.desc:
Rose Rejects is coffee that didn’t make it into our main lineup.
It’s a mix of beans rejected by our colour sorter — including quakers and beans that are visually over-roasted — alongside roasted batches that missed our internal targets by being too light, too dark, or otherwise outside spec. Nothing unsafe, nothing adulterated, just coffee that didn’t meet the standard we set for Rose.
This is not a curated blend and it’s not meant to be expressive or particularly tasty. Expect a very basic cup. Sometimes flat, sometimes rough, sometimes fine — but never special. If you’re looking for clarity

items.title: The House Blend
items.desc:
This is a special "House Blend" that we've designed specifically for use on Espresso machines / Bialetti. It's an easy drinking coffee that has a well developed roast profile to make it easy to extract, while still keeping recognisable flavours of the origins. We would call this a "Medium - Dark" roast. Not so much that the beans are all oily, but developed enough to have Low Acidity, Smooth Body, and mostly chocolatey flavour notes.
All the coffees we use in this are Specialty coffee, but with very approachable taste profiles and qualities. We've sourced these lots either direct from farmers,

items.title: The Bedtime Blend
items.desc:
This is a blend that we've designed especially to be as delicious as non-decaffeinated coffee - to be used for Espresso/Bialetti brewing and goes amazing as both a black coffee, and with milk.
We believe that decaffeinated coffee doesn't have to come at the sacrifice of quality - so we created this Decaf blend that is as delicious as full strength coffee. Generally you will find more sweetness and acidity, as the balance with the bitter caffeine has been removed. In some of these coffees we find more spice, and malt notes from the decaf process, and some darker roasted notes from the darker ro

items.title: Jingle Beans Holiday Blend
items.desc: Behold! A coffee is born. 'Tis the freaking season and what have you! Oh, Jingle Beans, oh Jingle Beans, our annual ho-li-day blend. Each year we go out of our way to make this blend as seasonally outlandish as we can. This year, two coffees from Ethiopia — a washed and a naturally processed — triumphantly coalesce into the best interpretation of drinkable fruit cake in a cup. Jingle Beans, Jingle Beans, Jingle all the beans.

items.title: David Muñoz - Honduras
items.desc: For the second consecutive year, we kick off Honduran season with a coffee from David Muñoz, a producer who’s been a mainstay on the Tandem menu for a decade. David grows multiple varieties on his roughly 3 hectare farm, Nueva Esperanza, in Santa Barbara, but the majority is Pacas. This 100% Pacas lot is soft and sweetness-driven. We taste a familiar, balanced cup with flavors of caramel, milk chocolate, toasted nuts, and gentle plum-like acidity.

items.title: Arley Arboleda - Colombia
items.desc: This small lot from Arley Arboleda is another excellent Chiroso from Urrao. Arley is a 36-year-old, second-generation producer growing Chiroso at 2,100 masl across two hectares. He learned coffee farming from his father as a teenager and purchased the land for Finca Los Guaicos in 2022 with the specific goal of cultivating exclusively Chiroso. As with many producers in the region, Arley uses the cochadas method, a regional processing practice in which each day’s harvest is depulped and added to the same fermentation tank throughout the week. Once the tank is full, the coffee is washed together

items.title: Chelbesa - Ethiopia
items.desc: We’re excited to have back on our menu for another season this bright, refreshing classic from the Chelbesa One Washing Station. Approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers deliver cherry to Chelbesa One, one of seven washing stations across Ethiopia managed by SNAP Coffee. Cherries are sorted, floated, and depulped, then dry fermented in tanks for 48-72 hours before being washed and placed to dry on raised beds for 7-10 days. Coffees from this station are typically pristine and elegant. Expect a crisp, lightly effervescent profile with white tea aromatics and flavors of grapefruit, melon, and pea

items.title: Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: This washed field blend from Kibingo Estate is another stellar coffee sourced via Kamavindi Coffee Labs. Established in 1957 with just 100 trees — the maximum allotment for Kenyan growers under colonial law at the time — Kibingo has since grown into one of the country’s most highly regarded estate farms. The estate won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition in 2024, and owner Anthony Kimani has continued investing in farm-level and processing infrastructure, with plans to expand beyond its current 6,000 trees. In the cup, we taste ripe red fruits like pomegranate and raspberry, sweet spice, and

items.title: Oneska - Kenya
items.desc: Oneska is the small estate farm of Onesmus Njagi, a retired schoolteacher, and his wife, Karen, on the slopes of Mount Kenya in Embu County. Last fall, we visited ahead of harvest and toured their four hectares, where they grow the traditional SL-28 and SL-34 varieties at good altitude and under ideal growing conditions. The name Oneska is a portmanteau of Onesmus and Karen, who established the farm in the early 1990s and have spent decades honing their agronomic and processing practices. They process their coffee using the classic Kenyan “double fermentation”: 20 hours of dry fermentation fol

items.title: Heri Agena - Ethiopia
items.desc: This microlot is the first of four coffees we’ll feature this year from Karamo Coffee, a quality-driven export company working in the high-altitude regions of Bensa and Bura in Sidama. We met Teddy of Karamo in Addis Ababa last year for a quick cupping and were very impressed by the quality of the coffees on the table. Teddy started Karamo in 2020, after his family’s farm won that year’s inaugural Ethiopian Cup of Excellence with a natural lot called “Karamo.” Farmers contributing to Karamo’s lots grow local heirloom varieties at extraordinary elevations, where production is limited but qualit

items.title: Danche Yellow Honey- Ethiopia
items.desc: This honey-processed Ethiopian coffee comes to us from Danche station in Gedeb, one of two sites operated by SNAP Specialty Coffee in the kebele of Chelbesa. Founded in 2019, Danche now processes cherry from approximately 800 nearby smallholder farmers, most of whom grow small amounts of coffee on 2-3 hectare plots of land at significant elevation. Danche began with a focus on washed lots but has since expanded to include natural, honey, and experimental preparations. In the honey process, cherries are partially depulped, leaving a calibrated amount of fruit mucilage on the seeds. Honeys are o

items.title: Alma Pineda - Cup of Excellence - Honduras
items.desc: This year, we purchased a split share of Alma Pineda’s washed Gesha lot, one of our top-scoring coffees from the 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence (CoE). Alma’s coffees have placed at the Honduras CoE before, including third in 2019 and second in 2024, with this lot placing eighth in the Exotic Varieties category. Her farm, El Limo, sits at 1650 masl in Santa Barbara, where nearly all the Honduran coffee on our menu is grown. Alma received the land from her father in 2012, and after a year working abroad to save money, she returned home to invest in her farms and coffees. Her Gesha is a stellar

items.title: Faver Ninco - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first of three Pink Bourbon lots we’ll be featuring from the main harvest at Finca Costa Rica, Faver Ninco’s 10-hectare farm in Santa Maria. At just over 2,000 masl, Finca Costa Rica experiences cooler temperatures than much of the region, with more limited sunlight and less regular rainfall. These factors combine to produce more sporadic flowering and nearly year-round picking. Within that fluid cycle, Finca Costa Rica still has a defined main harvest season that runs from May to August, with this first lot coming from the early and peak portions of the harvest. This coffee presen

items.title: Sun Lamp Decaf
items.desc:
“I might as well be drinking tea*,” you say to no one in particular as you drink another cup of lousy decaffeinated coffee. Don’t feel defeated by bad decaf. Turn to Tandem’s brighter, sweeter Sun Lamp. With hints of marshmallow, graham cracker and green grape, let the surprising flavors of Sun Lamp reimagine what decaffeinated coffee can be and leave the anxiety behind.
*No offense to tea. We love tea.

items.title: West End Blues
items.desc: Traditional in name only, West End Blues is a complex blend of flavors and textures. Fruity but not fruit-forward, grounded in chocolate and sparkling with zesty notes of baking spices and tea, WEB shines when combined with milk but stands on its own as a killer drip coffee.

items.title: Stoker
items.desc: Sometimes you want a delicious, no-nonsense cup of coffee, beloved by metalheads and hardcore grandmothers alike. That’s why Tandem shed its “Light Roaster” mantle to create our version of a “Kinda Dark” roasted coffee. Inspired by late-night diner runs, hot donuts, and arctic blasts, Stoker’s pleasantly sweet roastiness will carry you through the day.

items.title: Time & Temperature
items.desc: Effervescent, electric, and just plain cool, Time and Temperature is Tandem’s signature espresso blend. Perfect for dancing alone or with friends, it doubles as a delightful drip coffee. However you enjoy its crisp acidity and punchy sweetness, it’s our embodiment of “Spreading Joy” in every cup.
